themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On durable identity resolution today, Claude proposed recruiting a few thousand people who list every device they use as a truth set, while earlier answers on answer engine optimization, cross-channel incrementality, B2B buying-group signal loss, and generative content governance all said the measuring instrument drifts or no reliable answer key exists.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: All three models called ad platforms and trained models black boxes on provable downstream consent and deletion, and on identity resolution Gemini said the platforms that control devices earn more by keeping their walls up than by letting outsiders match people across them.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every answer on safe agent execution put a proxy, gateway, or broker in front of martech writes with hard spend and audience caps, and the consent enforcement answers did the same by forcing all data exits through a single checkpoint with expiring audience feeds.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay instead of writing another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models all proposed a fast lane with better data or prices so declaring beats spoofing, journey orchestration stalls on channel owners paid for their own conversions, and the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions a political settlement rather than a modeling gap.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than trying to remove it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three narrow generation to a registry of pre-approved claims because deciding if wording is supported stays a human judgment, and on the semantic context layer and journey orchestration they say there is no single correct definition of customer or of a good outcome.
